facts.text: Viking 2 Seismometer was deployed at Utopia Planitia during Viking 2 in 1976.

A three-axis inertial seismometer mounted atop the lander bus. Unlike Viking 1 whose sensor locking pins failed to release, Viking 2's locking mechanism successfully uncaged, allowing it to record planetary ground accelerations.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Recorded background seismic noise caused by Martian atmospheric wind gusts and detected one possible genuine magnitude 2.8 marsquake on Sol 80.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Utopia Planitia.
Provided humanity's first direct seismic data from the interior of Mars, setting the technical benchmark for the InSight mission 42 years later.
